parent_objective: verify profile separability before longer L0/L1/L2/L3 comparison
blocked_by: M1200 classifies L2 window-equivalence as inconclusive but suspicious and L3 reset parity as negative for hidden benefit in M1199
supersedes: running a longer comparison before checking whether profiles are meaningfully separated
invalidates: treating M1199 L2 trend as ready for direct scaling without implementation and action-sensitivity audit

public_gates: M1201 may run artifact and checkpoint analysis only
M1201 must not run candidate replay
M1201 must not use private holdout
M1201 must not claim paper-level evidence or self-identification
forbidden_shortcuts: do not claim profile superiority from action probes
do not add hidden or oracle actor inputs

workflow_synthesis.evidence_axis: G_profile_separability: L2 window and L3 hidden-state action sensitivity
workflow_synthesis.evidence_increment: checks whether M1199 profile families are actually separated enough to justify a longer comparison
workflow_synthesis.claim_scope: artifact/action-sensitivity audit only; no training promotion private-holdout paper-level generalization recurrent-belief or self-identification claim
stop_condition: stop if L2 profile configs or rollout observations do not differ as intended
stop if L2 trained policies are insensitive to older-history ablation
stop if L3 reset-hidden actions match online hidden actions on audited states
stop if evaluation masking is inconsistent with training masking
fallback_plan: route to profile implementation repair if config or masking is wrong
route to history-necessity task design if profiles are correct but insensitive
route to longer repeated pilot only if profile separability is adequate
route to metric repair if M1199 aggregation is flawed
workflow_synthesis.synthesis_trigger: M1200 selects separability audit before any longer pilot

admission_evidence: M1199 public pilot completed without run failures
M1200 audits that M1199 trend is not sufficient for direct scaling
L2 window-equivalence and L3 reset-parity require artifact/action-sensitivity checks
blocked_shortcuts: do not make paper-level or self-ID claims
allowed_updates: status, queue, scoreboard, research log, review, and next manifest
next_stage_criteria: observation history stack differences are verified
L2 older-history ablation sensitivity is measured
L3 reset-hidden action sensitivity is measured

self_id_evidence_discipline.current_frame_substitution_risk: M1201 explicitly tests whether current-frame feedback is substituting for older history or recurrent hidden state, but it remains an artifact/action audit rather than a closed-loop self-ID proof.
self_id_evidence_discipline.temporal_evidence_window: Use M1199 checkpoints and public eval states; do not introduce private holdout or new training distributions.
self_id_evidence_discipline.negative_result_policy: If profiles are insensitive to older history or hidden state, route to task/profile design rather than lowering self-ID standards.
allowed_claims: action-level history sensitivity or insensitivity on public artifacts
no recurrent-belief, strong self-identification, promotion, private-holdout, real-vehicle, or paper-result claim

hypothesis: M1199 profile families can be audited for config, observation, and action-level separability before any longer comparison.
success_criteria: L2 older-history action sensitivity is measured or a tooling blocker is recorded
L3 reset-hidden action sensitivity is measured or a tooling blocker is recorded
no training, PPO, candidate replay, promotion, private holdout, per-profile tuning, or actor-input contract change occurs
failure_criteria: M1201 treats action probes as paper-level evidence
hidden or oracle actor inputs are introduced
audit skips L2 or L3 separability

commands.name: audit_profile_separability
commands.command: analyze M1199 configs, checkpoints, and public eval states without training

decision_rule: M1201 passes if it audits M1199 profile separability and chooses a safe next route without training, tuning, promotion, private holdout, or claim expansion.
